questions.question: If a package of explosives has an oily stain or looks wet, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: Never transport damaged explosives. Do not accept packages that are wet or have oily stains.

questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, which action should you avoid?
questions.explanation: When loading corrosive materials by hand, load each container carefully one at a time. Keep containers upright. Do not drop or roll them.

questions.question: What must a box display if it contains liquid containers?

options.text: Arrows showing which way is up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows showing which way is up.
questions.explanation: Boxes with liquid containers must have arrows that show the correct upright direction.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty hazmat cargo tanks, what must you do at a railroad crossing?

options.text: You should not cross the railroad.
You should slow down but don't have to stop.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle has hazmat cargo tanks, you must stop at railroad crossings. This rule applies whether the tanks are full or empty.

questions.question: After a hazmat accident, which action is NOT your responsibility as the driver?

options.text: Keeping people away from the area.
Trying to put the fire out yourself.
Telling emergency workers about the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trying to put the fire out yourself.
questions.explanation: Your duties after a hazmat accident include keeping people away, limiting material spread if safe, and informing emergency personnel about the materials. Do not fight hazmat fires yourself unless you have proper equipment and training.

questions.question: Are shipping papers required for hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers are required for every hazardous materials shipment to communicate the risks.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials warning placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: What could indicate that cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo comes from a supermarket.
The cargo is on wood pallets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often contain hazardous materials. Take proper precautions when transporting such cargo.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The manual is a starting point. To learn more, read federal and state hazmat rules and take hazardous materials training courses.

questions.question: If you discover hazardous materials leaking while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to find a phone and call for help.
Leave the vehicle to find help elsewhere.

questions.explanation: If cargo is leaking, park as soon as possible. Continuing to drive spreads contamination and increases cleanup costs and danger.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they receive a leaking package or shipment?

options.text: Leave it on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse any leaking packages or shipments of hazardous materials.

questions.question: On shipping papers, the identification number, shipping name, and hazard class should:

options.text: Be abbreviated if using a small piece of paper.
Only be abbreviated if the abbreviations are easy to understand.

questions.explanation: These three items must never be abbreviated on hazardous materials shipping papers, unless the regulations specifically allow it.

questions.question: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a shipping paper, what placard must be shown?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on the shipping paper or package, you must display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: Who is responsible for labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, labeling, and supplying the warning placards for hazardous materials.

questions.question: Where should a placard be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: At least three inches away from any other markings.
Under a ladder, if space is an issue.
On a background that is a similar color to the placard.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least three inches away from any other markings.
questions.explanation: A placard must be placed at least three inches away from any other markings and away from doors and ladders. It should be placed on a background that contrasts with the placard.

questions.question: If you find that your cargo is leaking, what should you do?

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify the cargo.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
Assume all the cargo is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
questions.explanation: Use the shipping papers, labels, or package location to identify leaking materials. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, your vehicle should not be parked:
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle carrying these explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Do not park within five feet of the road's edge.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how should the hazardous materials be shown?

options.text: Circled by a pen or marker.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must be distinguished from non-hazardous materials by listing them first, highlighting them in a contrasting color, or marking them with an "X" in an "HM" column.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials warning placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: What should a driver check before transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare package markings and labels to the shipping papers. Make sure the shipper provided the correct description and proper labels.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be placed?

options.text: Easy to see when entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easy to see when entering the cab.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers for hazardous materials must be kept where the driver can reach them easily while wearing a seat belt. They must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: When can you move a vehicle that is not properly placarded?

options.text: If the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper hazardous materials placards cannot be driven except in an emergency to protect life and property.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, how far must you park from a building?
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a building, bridge, tunnel, gathering place, or open fire.

questions.question: What should you do with liquid discharge valves when loading compressed gas?
questions.explanation: Liquid discharge valves must be open during loading and unloading. They must be closed at all other times.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tire with your hand.

questions.explanation: You must check tire pressure before each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only effective way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: What should you do with the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids?
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. Only keep the engine running if you need it to operate a pump.

questions.question: How must you sign a hazardous waste manifest?

options.text: On the outside of the trailer.

questions.explanation: You must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest when transporting hazardous waste. It must be signed by hand.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials employees must be trained and tested at least once every three years.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do when loading hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake before loading or unloading. Keep hazardous materials away from heat. Do not use hooks or tools that could damage containers.
